messages:
jamal: Kicking off planning for the post-launch email cadence for the new Redwood Dispatch weekly. Need a drip matrix that routes inbound signals to the right sequence and SDR queues. Goal: 3-week nurture for trial -> paid conversion, plus a reengage path for cold lists. Thoughts on segments + send windows? :rocket:

elaine: Love it. My baseline: 4 segments — new_signups, active_trial (>=10 calls/day), low_usage_reengage, paid_customers. Each gets a 3-email mini-drip over 10 days. A/B subject on email #1, then personalize with product usage. :memo:

tanya: For inbound routing add a "high_signal" tag: api_calls > 100/24h OR dedicated instance created OR response_latency_alerts. High_signal -> SDR queue (1hr SLA). Otherwise route to automated nurture. We'll need Customer.io -> HubSpot webhook mapping and a fallback to email-only if HubSpot is down.

mike: Draft of segment rules (CSV sample):
```
segment_id,rule_description,criteria
new_signups,First 7 days from signup,created_at <= 7days
active_trial,High API usage,api_calls_24h >= 10
high_signal,Sales alert,api_calls_24h >= 100 OR instance_type = dedicated
low_usage_reengage,Low activity,last_30d_api_calls < 3
paid_customers,Paid plan,plan IN (pro,enterprise)
```

mike: Send windows proposal (by timezone):
```
- Americas: Tue/Thu 10:00 local
- EMEA: Wed 10:30 local
- APAC: Thu 09:00 local
- Reengage: Sat 11:00 local (test small %)
```

mike: UTM & tracking: add utm_source=dispatch&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=launch_week1 and tag events: email_open, cta_click, account_activation. Also append email_tag=launch2026 for filtering.

elaine: Subject line A/B ideas: A) "Redwood Dispatch: Faster LLM inference, real savings" B) "How teams cut inference costs by 2x — Redwood Dispatch" — run on 50/50 for 48hrs then pick winner. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

tanya: Suppression rules: suppress anyone who opened in last 7 days from reengage; suppress bounced/complained addresses. Add a 90-day reconsent flow for EU. Also include preference center link in footer.

jamal: Nice. Can we map the trigger flow to HubSpot properties? e.g., hubspot.lead_source = "newsletter_dispatch" and hubspot.signal = high_signal|medium|low. Tanya, can you paste webhook mapping?

tanya: Will do. Draft mapping below (Customer.io -> HubSpot webhook payload example):
```json
{
  "email": "{{customer.email}}",
  "lead_source": "newsletter_dispatch",
  "signal": "{{customer.vars.signal}}",
  "api_calls_24h": "{{customer.vars.api_calls_24h}}",
  "utm_campaign": "{{campaign.name}}"
}
```

tanya: If HubSpot returns 5xx -> retry 3x then mark event for manual QA.

jamal: Good. For SDR routing, we'll create a view "Dispatch - high_signals" and auto-assign to rotation. Mike, can you add the contact enrichment step (company size + cloud region) to the webhook?

mike: Yep — adding company_size + region. Also recommending a 10-email warmup span for new ip if we hit >10k sends/day; coordinate with eng-sre.

marketing-bot: Deliverability snapshot uploaded: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/drive-report (open) — inbox placement predicted 92% for first send, spam risk low.

elaine: Action items:
- tanya: publish webhook mapping and HubSpot property names (ETA EOD)
- mike: finalize segment CSV + send schedule + enrichment fields (ETA tomorrow)
- jamal: draft subject lines + experiment plan (ETA EOD)
- marketing: confirm ESP send limits and warmup with eng-sre (sync Wed)

jamal: Thanks all. We'll iterate on the drip matrix in this thread. If no objections, I'll move to a Google Sheet and start the Customer.io flows tomorrow. :thumbsup:
